claude.rationale: CUB merged whole into PacWest via direct statutory merger with a parallel bank-level merger, so the acquired legal vehicle terminated (T3) and PacWest's controlling intent was installed (T1 replace). The branch/delivery network (T4) and its operations (T5) were disclosed as being closed/consolidated on both sides — i.e., product and process were reorganized together into the combined network, so no product-vs-process mismatch (gap_45=0). Likewise, CUB's board and officers ceased at closing while operations were consolidated under PacWest's continuing directors/officers, with three CUB executives bridged via fixed-term consulting agreements — process and organization moved together into the acquirer's structure rather than one transferring without the other (gap_56=0), hence gap_mitigated NA.

grok.rationale: gap_45=0 because the slice ties product and process together under the parallel bank-level statutory merger of California United Bank into Pacific Western Bank, with only a disclosed plan to close/consolidate branches on both sides rather than any product-without-process split at closing (DEFM14A cover letter; branch-network risk factor). gap_56=1 because operational absorption of CU Bank into Pacific Western Bank occurred while CUB directors and executive officers expressly ceased at closing and PacWest’s pre-closing directors/officers continued, so target management/organization did not transfer alongside the processes; the only bridge was fixed-term post-closing consulting agreements with three CUB executives (DEFM14A Board/Officers and Consulting Agreements; 8-K Item 5.02), which contractually mitigate that gap.

openai.rationale: The disclosed closing structure combined CU Bank with Pacific Western Bank and contemplated reorganizing both sides of the branch/delivery network through reciprocal closures and consolidations, rather than transferring customer-facing branches without an accompanying operational structure [SRC: SEC accession 0001047469-17-004755, DEFM14A]. Although CUB's directors and executive officers ceased serving, PacWest's incumbent directors and officers continued at the surviving corporation and three CUB executives entered closing-conditioned consulting agreements; the slice documents management replacement and limited continuity, but not a process-versus-organization mismatch at closing [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-17-063201, Form 8-K Item 5.02; SEC accession 0001047469-17-004755, DEFM14A].
